---
title: "VG09 — Joint model with study and subject random intercepts on understood and production ratio: children with Down syndrome"
abstract: "*VG09 is the headline Down syndrome joint model. It extends VG08 with a parallel non-centred subject-level random intercept on the production ratio q. Between-subject SD on the production-ratio logit is the largest single variance component in the model family; VG08 was absorbing this into the spoken-side Beta-Binomial dispersion. VG09 wins the K=5 leave-one-subject-out comparison decisively against both VG07 and VG08 and is recommended for all Down syndrome reporting in this technical report — descriptive and predictive.*"
---

## Overview

The motivation for VG09 is symmetry. If between-subject differences justify a subject RE on the understood trajectory (VG08 vs VG07), the same logic applies to how much of each child's understood vocabulary they actually produce. The empirical result is striking: between-subject SD on the production-ratio logit ($\tau^{\text{subj}}_q \approx 1.20$) turns out to be the largest single variance component in the model family — larger than between-subject SD on understood (0.84), larger than either study-level SD (0.52 on understood, 0.94 on `q`), and much larger than what VG08's structure could express.

The model structure follows VG08 with one additional term on the production-ratio logit:

$$f_U(a, s, i) = \text{intercept}_U + \text{slope}_U \cdot a_z + g_U(a) + \delta_U[s] + \delta^{\text{subj}}_U[i]$$
$$h(a, s, i) = \text{intercept}_q + \text{slope}_q \cdot a_z + g_q(a) + \delta_q[s] + \delta^{\text{subj}}_q[i]$$

with $\delta^{\text{subj}}_U[i] = \tau^{\text{subj}}_U \cdot z^U_i$, $\delta^{\text{subj}}_q[i] = \tau^{\text{subj}}_q \cdot z^q_i$, $z^U_i, z^q_i \sim \mathrm{Normal}(0, 1)$ (both non-centred), $\tau^{\text{subj}}_U, \tau^{\text{subj}}_q \sim \mathrm{HalfNormal}(0.5)$.

## Results

### Variance partition: the full picture

Comparing the three successive DS joint models with REs:

| Variance component (logit-SD) | VG07 | VG08 | VG09 |
| :--- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Between-study ($\tau_U$, understood) | 0.50 | 0.51 | 0.52 |
| Between-study ($\tau_q$, q) | 0.66 | 0.74 | 0.94 |
| Between-subject ($\tau^{\text{subj}}_U$, understood) | — | 0.78 | **0.84** |
| Between-subject ($\tau^{\text{subj}}_q$, q) | — | — | **1.20** |
| Spoken BB dispersion ($a_{\kappa,S}$, log) | 1.40 | 1.86 | **3.32** |
| Understood BB dispersion ($a_{\kappa,U}$, log) | 1.75 | 2.93 | 3.10 |

Each successive model shrinks the residual Beta-Binomial dispersion (higher $a_\kappa$ = less overdispersion) by reassigning variability to its proper structural source. The spoken-side dispersion factor at mid-age moves from $\exp(1.40) \approx 4.0$ (VG07) → $\exp(1.86) \approx 6.4$ (VG08) → $\exp(3.32) \approx 27.6$ (VG09): an order-of-magnitude reduction in residual within-occasion overdispersion.

Between-subject SD on the production-ratio logit of 1.20 corresponds, on the count scale, to a typical DS child's `q` sitting anywhere in roughly a fivefold range around the population median at matched comprehension. That heterogeneity was invisible in VG07 and VG08; under VG09 it has its own well-identified parameter (ESS_bulk ≈ 7 000, r̂ = 1.001).

### Population trajectory

Median values (population-level trajectory; $\delta_U[s] = \delta_q[s] = \delta^{\text{subj}}_U[i] = \delta^{\text{subj}}_q[i] = 0$), with 90% credible intervals:

| Age (months) | Understood (median) | Spoken (median) | Production ratio (q) |
| ---: | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 12 | 20 [13–28] | 0.2 [0.1–0.4] | 0.01 |
| 24 | 89 [67–113] | 7 [3–10] | 0.07 |
| 36 | 186 [145–227] | 49 [28–71] | 0.26 |
| 48 | 257 [207–309] | 168 [123–212] | 0.66 |
| 60 | 344 [284–407] | 290 [235–346] | 0.85 |
| 72 | 438 [365–512] | 389 [328–453] | 0.90 |
| 84 | 509 [411–600] | 434 [358–510] | 0.87 |

Two things change relative to VG08:

- The population-level `q` rises *higher* through the middle of the age range (q ≈ 0.85 at 60 months, ~0.90 at 72 months) before settling around 0.87–0.90 in the older ages, rather than plateauing at 0.79–0.84 as VG08 suggested. The reason is the same Simpson's-paradox logic that drove the VG07 → VG08 shift for the understood trajectory: VG08's `q` was being pulled toward observation density, which over-weighted children with high comprehension but lower-than-typical production. VG09's subject RE on `q` absorbs that variability.
- The early-age `q` is *lower* than VG07 and VG08 (0.07 at 24 months versus 0.14 for both VG07 and VG08). A typical young DS child speaks even fewer of the words they understand than the previous models suggested.

### Why VG09 is the headline DS joint model

Three leave-one-subject-out (LOSO) comparisons were run on 13 May 2026 in increasing order of methodological rigour. Full details are in the [model comparison chapter](model-comparison.qmd); the headline numbers are:

| Quantity | VG07 | VG08 | VG09 |
| :--- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Conditional LOSO elpd (RE at posterior estimate) | −8 740 | −8 360 | **−8 152** |
| K-fold LOSO elpd (K = 5, refit per fold, RE drawn from prior at MCMC time) | −8 753 | −8 524 | **−8 414** |

The K-fold row is the gold standard. Standard errors on the totals are 252, 242 and 236 respectively; paired-difference SEs are 26 (VG07 → VG08), 19 (VG08 → VG09) and 35 (VG07 → VG09). Every pairwise diff/dSE is above 5.7 — overwhelmingly significant. VG09 wins decisively both as a *description* of the DS data we have AND as a *predictor* of a brand-new DS child.

::: {.callout-note title="Earlier marginal LOSO finding superseded"}

An earlier (12 May 2026) marginal LOSO computation appeared to favour VG07 decisively for unseen-child prediction (VG09 elpd of −22 565 vs VG07 elpd of −14 151). A sanity check exposed the problem: for VG07 (which has no subject RE) the marginal LOSO must equal the conditional LOSO mathematically, but the recomputed pipeline returned −14 151 against the conditional −8 740. The 5 400-elpd discrepancy was driven by PSIS-LOO instability on the thinned posterior plus Monte Carlo noise in the Beta-Binomial recomputation. The K-fold result, which refits each model on each training fold and so does not depend on PSIS, is what supersedes the marginal computation. The earlier marginal numbers should not be cited.
:::

The K-fold result also resolves the underlying theoretical question: adding subject REs and shrinking the Beta-Binomial dispersion does *not* compromise generalisation to an unseen DS child, because the priors on the subject REs ($\tau^{\text{subj}}_U \approx 0.84$, $\tau^{\text{subj}}_q \approx 1.20$) are wide enough to span the actual range of between-subject variability. The posterior predictive distribution for a held-out subject is a Beta-Binomial whose `p` is itself a wide mixture over the subject-RE prior; the resulting mixture is empirically broader than VG07's single Beta-Binomial despite VG09's lower within-occasion $\kappa$.

### Subject-marginalised posterior predictive distribution

The count distributions, PMF/CDF, median-trend plots and the `Y_*` and `P(Y ≤ k)` columns in the per-model posterior summary tables integrate over both subject random-effect priors ($\tau^{\text{subj}}_U \approx 0.84$, $\tau^{\text{subj}}_q \approx 1.20$). This is the correct predictive distribution to compare with an unseen DS child's expected vocabulary counts. The latent probability columns (`p_median`, `Ey_median`) are unchanged from the population-level estimates because those describe the latent mean rather than the predictive spread.

### Headline matched-comprehension finding

Under VG09, the production ratio `q` rises from ~0.04 at 100 understood words to ~0.85 at 300 understood words and ~0.88 at 500. A typical typically-developing child speaks about half the words they understand by the time they understand ~120 words; a typical DS child reaches the same milestone at ~226 understood words. Children with Down syndrome accumulate roughly **1.85× as much** receptive vocabulary before their spoken vocabulary catches up, at every threshold checked between q = 0.25 and q = 0.90. See @sec-matched-comprehension in the [model comparison chapter](model-comparison.qmd) for the full table and the DS/TD overlay.

### Diagnostics

VG09 sampled at rep quality (6 chains × 6 000 + 6 000 NUTS, target_accept = 0.95): r̂_max = 1.002, ESS_bulk_min = 1 841 across reported parameters, zero divergences, 18 m 57 s wall time.

## Status of VG09 in the family

VG09 is the headline DS joint model recommended for all Down syndrome reporting in this technical report — both descriptive (cleanest variance partition, sharpest within-subject growth trajectory, biggest conditional-LOSO win) and predictive for an unseen DS child (largest K-fold LOSO elpd, diff/dSE close to 10 against VG07). When the report quotes specific values for typical DS understood and spoken word counts, the production ratio, milestone ages or matched-comprehension comparisons, they come from VG09 unless otherwise indicated.

For full per-model output see `output/models/VG09-age-understood-spoken-ds-re-subj-uq/index.html`.
